header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood SE), Dana Lopez (WestBridge InfoSec), Michael Carter (WestBridge Platform), Sara Kim (WestBridge PM), Evan Ruiz (WestBridge Infra)
summary: Weekly POC security sync. Reviewed SSO/SAML setup, audit log retention and export, SOC 2 artifacts, KMS/encryption questions, and next steps to run on-prem connectivity test. Agreed to share SOC2 and pen test, Priya to share SSO metadata, Jordan to run VPN test the following week. Some clarifications on log retention windows and RBAC scope; performance/latency concerns deferred to separate SE deep-dive.
topics: SSO / SAML setup, audit logs & SIEM export, data retention / KV cache logs, SOC2 artifacts and pen-test, KMS / encryption for logs, RBAC and org-level access, private deployment connectivity (VPN), next steps and action owners
transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood, um we are on for the weekly P O C security sync with WestBridge. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Dana: Dana Lopez here, InfoSec.
[00:10] Michael: Michael Carter, platform.
[00:13] Sara: Sara Kim, product.
[00:15] Evan: Evan Ruiz, infra.
[00:17] Priya: Priya Nair, SE on the Redwood side. Jordan on as well.
[00:22] Jordan: Hey all.
[00:25] Alex: Great, thanks. Agenda — SSO status, audit logs/retention, SOC two artifacts follow-up, and plan VPN test for private connectivity. Anything else?
[00:34] Dana: Could we spend extra time on the retention part, and how long audit logs are available in the hosted stack? That's critical for our compliance team.
[00:42] Alex: Totally. Priya, do you want to start on SSO?
[00:46] Priya: Sure. We pushed earlier this week the SAML metadata to your Okta tenant as discussed, there was one squiggle in the entity id, um WestBridge's metadata expects urn:westbridge:apps but our default was redwood:prod, so we provided a mapping in the metadata. Michael, did that hit you okay?
[01:05] Michael: Yeah I saw that, there was an error at first because of the assertion consumer service URL, we fixed the ACS on our side. Logging showed a couple failed logins, but they were from test accounts.
[01:18] Priya: Cool, good. For the POC we support SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows, SLO is not implemented in the hosted POC path yet, just to flag.
[01:27] Dana: SLO is okay to omit for now, but we need to know how session invalidation is recorded — like if a user is removed from Okta will access be revoked quickly?
[01:37] Priya: Yes, our session TTL honors the SAML assertion lifetime and we have a TTL of 8 hours by default for the hosted demo; we can shorten that for your pilot. We can also do a periodic user sync via SCIM in the next phase.
[01:50] Sara: Can you shorten it to 1 hour? Our policy wants short-lived sessions for admin roles.
[01:55] Priya: Yes we can set role TTLs — admin role can be set to 1 hour, regular users to 8. We'll include the config snippets in the doc.
[02:04] Alex: Good. Next: audit logs. Michael, can you tell us what WestBridge needs for SIEM ingestion?
[02:11] Michael: We need audit logs for all admin and system actions, with user id, timestamp, IP, event type, and request payloads where possible. Retention for cold storage is seven years, but for hot SIEM we want 90 days. Also need a streaming export, ideally via S3 export or syslog to our collector.
[02:28] Jordan: Redwood supports both S3 export and a webhook/stream to a customer collector. Our audit logs are JSON lines with event category, user, timestamp, request_id, and optional payload. We currently keep 30 days in-app and export the rest to S3.
[02:41] Dana: 30 days in-app is too short. Can you bump to 90 for the pilot? Or at least ensure immediate export to our S3 bucket under our control?
[02:50] Jordan: We can immediately configure daily exports to your S3 bucket; bucket must have cross-account access and an encryption policy. For the in-app retention, increasing to 90 has a unit-cost implication — but for the POC we're fine to do it as an exception.
[03:05] Michael: Great, we'll provide the S3 ARN and role. Also need the manifest format for the exporter so our SIEM team can parse.
[03:13] Priya: We'll send the exporter manifest and schema; it's basically ndjson with event_type, user, ts, ip, request_id, payload. We'll include an example.
[03:21] Alex: On the subject of payloads — we do redact sensitive user inputs by default in hosted unless the customer opts-in to store raw inputs. Dana, is WestBridge okay with redaction?
[03:33] Dana: For banking PII we need redaction, yes. For troubleshooting the POC we may allow unredacted access via a secure, time-bound process.
[03:41] Priya: We have an audit workflow for that — request, approver, and time-limited unredact window. That will be recorded in the audit logs.
[03:50] Sara: And are the logs encrypted at rest?
[03:53] Jordan: Yes, S3 exports will be server-side encrypted and within Redwood we use envelope encryption with customer KMS option for dedicated/private deployments. For hosted we have Redwood-managed KMS by default; you can bring-your-own-KMS in private mode.
[04:07] Dana: For POC we want to test BYOK for log encryption, if possible.
[04:11] Alex: We can do BYOK in the private deployment. For the hosted POC we can simulate with a dedicated key or provide a short-term key exchange. We'll outline options in the docs.
[04:22] Evan: Quick question on KV cache logs — are those included in the audit export? We saw references in the docs to KV cache and prefix caching.
[04:30] Priya: KV cache hits/misses are emitted as metric events; request payloads and responses are logged per policy. We can include KV cache metadata in the audit export if you want, but usually it's filtered to reduce noise.
[04:42] Michael: We want traceability for cached responses for regulatory QA, at least for audit runs. If it's cheap to include a flag in the manifest to include KV metadata that would be ideal.
[04:52] Priya: Yep we'll add that flag to the exporter manifest — it's an opt-in field.
[04:57] Dana: Can you also confirm retention for cached items? There's a separate retention policy for caches.
[05:03] Jordan: Cache TTL is configurable per-model; default is 24 hours for prefix cache, but for the POC we can set to 7 days if needed. Note that cache retention is separate from audit log retention.
[05:14] Alex: Onto SOC 2 — Dana I know you asked for the certificate and controls mapping. We have a SOC 2 Type II report and a controls matrix. Alex: we'll share the report and the redwood controls mapping doc tonight.
[05:28] Dana: Awesome. Also, any recent pen-test results? We need a summary and remediation timeline.
[05:33] Alex: Yes, we ran a pen-test Q4 2025, there's a summary and remediation notes — nothing high-sev outstanding. I'll attach the pen-test summary to the shared folder.
[05:42] Dana: Sometimes the transcript bot mis-says SOC two as sock two, just flagging for clarity.
[05:47] (laughter)
[05:50] Alex: Noted.
[05:53] Sara: About RBAC — we need admin separation by team and a way to scope model rollout access so product can't flip model weights for production customers. Is that supported?
[06:03] Priya: Yes we have org-level roles, per-route roles, and model pinning controls. You can restrict model rollout to a specific flag or to certain users only. Changes are logged and require approver in dedicated/private setups.
[06:18] Michael: What about automated fallback? If a pinned model is unhealthy do you fall back to a lower-latency variant or does it block traffic?
[06:26] Jordan: We support automated fallback to configured compatible model variants and can route by policy. For the POC we recommend a canary + automated fallback with alerts.
[06:36] Dana: For compliance we want to see an audit trail of the fallback decision and routing policy change. Is that included?
[06:43] Priya: Yes, routing decision events are in the audit log with request_id and chosen_variant.
[06:49] Alex: Last major item: connectivity for private deployments. Jordan can you outline the VPN test plan?
[06:56] Jordan: We'll do a connectivity smoke test — site-to-site VPN, cert exchange, basic API handshake, then run a small throughput test with non-prod models. We'll provide a checklist: firewall ports, routing, DNS entries, and a contact window for the test. Suggested date next Wednesday.
[07:12] Evan: Next Wednesday works, we'll unblock the firewall and provide a test subnet.
[07:17] Jordan: Great. We'll also bring an ops runbook and a quick escalation path.
[07:22] Alex: Ok let's recap action items. Priya will send SAML metadata and example IdP config; Alex will share SOC2 and pen test; Jordan will schedule VPN test and share checklist; Michael will provide S3 ARN and SIEM manifest requirements. Any other open questions?
[07:36] Dana: One small ask — can we get a short doc on the unredact workflow and approver audit?
[07:42] Priya: Yes, we'll include the unredact workflow doc in the packet.
[07:46] Sara: Thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[07:49] Alex: Thanks all, we'll follow up via the shared folder and send calendar invite for the VPN test.
[07:54] (meeting ends)
